difficulty_reason: Given a solid diagram of module-valued functors with L linearly adequate, an exact row A^{n} -> A^{m} and a map L -> M, the lemma asserts the existence of the dotted lifting (statement lines 604-618). The proof constructs the lifting explicitly: with the matrix presentation of the row it forms the graded algebra B = A[x_1, ..., x_n]/(sum a_ij x_j), observes that the tuple (x_1, ..., x_n) descends to a unique element xi of L(B) with a universal property -- every element of L(C) is the image of xi along some algebra map -- and then uses the weight decomposition of the functors over the graded algebra B to see that phi(xi) lies in M tensor_A B_1, so that it can be written as a finite sum of m_i tensor x_i, which defines the required map A^{n} -> M (proof lines 620-643). The level is H3: a short but genuinely constructed proof, with the universal property of xi identified and exploited.
